messages:
Maya: heads up — we had a preemptible GPU eviction in us-west-2 at 14:02 that forced two streaming requests into fallback. seeing a small spike in failed token continuation acknowledgements.
Devon: saw that, a few traces: the handler attempted to stream cutover to the fallback replica but client-side ack timed out. logs show 'kv-cache-mismatch' for one session.
Ash: timeline? was the drain grace-window honored?
Maya: VM received SIGTERM, cloud provider gave 30s preemptible notice. our graceful-drain is 20s, so we started cutover at ~10s remaining. some requests had been mid-token and didn't get final ack before the instance disappeared.
Loren: that's the classic half-commit problem. we should avoid dropping in-flight tokens — propose we do a two-phase cutover: 1) stream checkpoint + flush prefix, 2) re-route new requests, 3) allow token tail to finish or requeue if not acknowledged.
Devon: agree on two-phase. also need jittered requeue so we don't stampede backend when many instances get evicted in same AZ. propose requeue-backoff config: initial=50ms, max=2s with exp jitter.
Ash: can we piggyback on existing requeue queue? we currently requeue at the request router but it assumes stateless retry. streaming sessions have KV cache that must be transferred or resumed.
Maya: idea: emit a short 'stream-snapshot' blob with last-kv pointers to object storage during drain. fallback can attempt fast-attach by pulling that blob. small extra egress but saves full recompute.
Devon: sketch of handler (pseudo):
```
onSIGTERM() {
  markInstanceState(DRAINING);
  for each live stream session {
    snapshot = dumpPrefixKV(session, last_n=8);
    upload(snapshot, s3://stream-checkpoints/<session-id>);
    publish(routing, session.id => fallback_candidates);
  }
  startRequestCutover(); // route new traffic off this machine
  wait(min(grace_window_remaining, MAX_WAIT_FOR_TAIL));
  forceCloseRemaining();
}
```
Ash: two follow-ups: 1) snapshot size limit — limit to 8 KV entries or 4KB to keep upload latency predictable. 2) secure ephemeral upload: sign URL per-upload; no long-lived creds.
Loren: for client compatibility, add a soft-resume API: client includes resume_token and server tries attach() to restore KV chain. if attach fails within 300ms, server returns requeue hint and a small resume payload location.
sre-bot: incident: stream-session-leak detected. opened ticket RINF-1209, notify @oncall.
Maya: concerns about cost: frequent snapshot uploads could add egress and S3 ops for high churn pools. we should gate snapshotting to mixed-capacity pools and preemptible-only workers with eviction rate > threshold.
Devon: alternative cheaper option: keep snapshot in ephemeral local NVMe attached to preemptible instance and coordinate via a tiny metadata service (fast attach within same AZ). if fallback in different AZ, fall back to S3.
Ash: network edge case: if cutover candidate is in same instance group but overloaded, we should prefer cross-pool routing to cold (reserved) backfills. routing policy: pref local-attach -> same-pool warm -> reserved capacity.
Loren: need to define SLA semantics: if we requeue a streaming tail, what does the client expect? propose 'at-least-once' for token generation tails, with dedupe via global request-id on resume. document in client SDK.
Maya: action items:
- Devon: prototype snapshot+attach flow (POC) and perf for upload < 100ms for 99p. due EOD Friday.
- Ash: add requeue backoff config + stampede protection in router. due next week.
- Loren: draft SDK resume API and dedupe semantics. due Thurs.
- Ops: enable stream-checkpointing only for preemptible pools for now.
Devon: I'll add metrics: checkpoint_upload_latency, attach_success_rate, resume_requeues.
Maya: also add alert when more than N sessions emit snapshots in a 30s window in an AZ — likely a mass-evict.
Loren: one last note — if eviction notice < 5s, don't attempt snapshot; immediately publish requeue hint and let client do a cold rehydrate. we can't gamble on a partial upload.
Ash: acked. small PR to add the <5s fast-fail path.
Maya: thanks all. I'll post a short design doc once Devon's POC numbers are in. :thumbsup:
